decision_rule.claim_pass: PASS requires a primary or formal source whose verified text supports the bounded claim, an exact page or section locator, a complete citation with DOI or stable URL, explicit non-support boundaries, and a project operationalization that is not attributed back to the source.
decision_rule.needs_source: NEEDS_SOURCE is mandatory when neither an exact primary-source PDF page nor an exact publisher/author-institution HTML section was directly verified. An abstract section can support only the bounded claim stated by that abstract. No page number may be inferred from the article page range.
decision_rule.overall_pass: PASS requires every named literature claim to have verified primary-source support and every project-designed control to be labeled as an operationalization with explicit scope and limitations. A project control does not require a source that prescribes the identical workflow unless this project claims that the control has measured effectiveness, guarantees error detection, or recovers ground truth.
decision_rule.quote_policy: A short quotation is stored only when the reviewer directly verified that text in a publisher, standards-body, institutional-repository, author-hosted, or repository-local copy of the original source.

verdict.reason: Every named topic has a bounded claim with an exact primary-source locator and an explicit non-support boundary. The three-track review, pane5 arbitration, implication labels, status taxonomy and positive-control construction remain disclosed project operationalizations. Their independent effectiveness has not been measured and is not claimed; this is a method limitation, not a missing citation for a literature claim.

citation.title: The Oracle Problem in Software Testing: A Survey

locator.access_level: Full IEEE published PDF verified; the PDF identifies the article as CC BY 3.0.

short_quote.text: The ground truth oracle, G, is a total test oracle that always gives the “right answer”.
short_quote.verified_from: IEEE published PDF, printed page 510, Section 2.3, Definition 2.6
short_quote.quote_supports: The excerpt distinguishes a conceptual ground-truth oracle from an implemented or observed oracle; adjacent Definitions 2.7-2.8 on the same page define the two implication directions.
short_quote.quote_does_not_support: The excerpt does not identify this ledger, an LLM reviewer, majority voting, or pane5 arbitration as ground truth.

supports: Representing oracle adequacy as directional implication rather than an unlabeled similarity judgment.
Retaining partial/proxy or unsupported outcomes rather than forcing every issue to an exact Boolean oracle.
Keeping an observed backend verdict distinct from conceptual ground truth.
does_not_support: That the ledger, a model, or an LLM reviewer is automatically the ground-truth oracle.
That three internal reviewers are statistically or epistemically independent.
That majority vote or pane5 arbitration recovers the right answer.
Any project-specific mapping among EQUIVALENT, O_IMPLIES_P, P_IMPLIES_O, and final gold statuses.
claim_to_source_matrix.project_operationalization: For Boolean obligation O and candidate P, exact gold requires both implication directions. A defective-side false proxy is sound only under O_IMPLIES_P, because P=false then entails O=false. P_IMPLIES_O is not a sound false proxy. This implication convention is a project-level logical operationalization, not Barr's nomenclature.

claim_to_source_matrix.claim: A temporal property may pass trivially when an implication antecedent is unsatisfiable, leaving the consequent irrelevant to the truth value; a true verdict therefore needs a non-vacuity check when implication-like structure is present.

claim_to_source_matrix.claim: UML StateMachines dispatch Event occurrences one at a time and complete a run-to-completion step at a stable configuration; an event with no enabled transition may be discarded, while an event that triggers orthogonal transitions is fully consumed only after those transitions finish.

citation.title: OMG Unified Modeling Language (OMG UML), Version 2.5.1

short_quote.text: Event occurrences are detected, dispatched, and processed by the StateMachine execution, one at a time.
short_quote.verified_from: Official OMG UML 2.5.1 PDF, page 316, Clause 14.2.3.9.1

supports: An explicit RTC observation point and stable-configuration boundary.
Separating dispatch, discard, enabled-transition execution, and full consumption.
Rejecting an observer that silently defines every consumed event as a nonempty committed-transition list without a declared profile.
does_not_support: A tool-neutral equality between event consumption and one specific runtime receipt field.
A total dispatch order, because UML leaves event-pool scheduling order undefined.
A single-transition assumption across orthogonal Regions.
Any conclusion about the author's intended response for a ledger issue.

claim_to_source_matrix.topic: UML Region completion, StateMachine completion, and terminate pseudostate semantics
claim_to_source_matrix.claim: A FinalState signifies completion of its enclosing Region. Completion of one Region directly contained in a StateMachine entails completion of the entire StateMachine Behavior only when all other Regions in that StateMachine are also complete. Entering a terminate Pseudostate instead terminates the StateMachine execution immediately without exiting active States or performing exit Behaviors, and aborts executing doActivities. These notions are not implied merely by an ordinary State having no outgoing Transition.

citation.title: OMG Unified Modeling Language (OMG UML), Version 2.5.1

short_quote.text: FinalState is a special kind of State signifying that the enclosing Region has completed.
short_quote.verified_from: Official OMG UML 2.5.1 PDF, page 312, Clause 14.2.3.6

additional_verified_quotes.text: If the enclosing Region is directly contained in a StateMachine and all other Regions in that StateMachine also are completed, then it means that the entire StateMachine behavior is completed.
additional_verified_quotes.verified_from: Official OMG UML 2.5.1 PDF, page 346, Clause 14.5.2.1

additional_verified_quotes.text: Entering a terminate Pseudostate implies that the execution of the StateMachine is terminated immediately.
additional_verified_quotes.verified_from: Official OMG UML 2.5.1 PDF, page 313, Clause 14.2.3.7

additional_verified_quotes.text: A FinalState cannot have any outgoing Transitions.
additional_verified_quotes.verified_from: Official OMG UML 2.5.1 PDF, page 346, Clause 14.5.2.5

supports: Separating Region-local FinalState completion from completion of the entire StateMachine Behavior.
Separating normal completion from immediate terminate-pseudostate semantics and external asynchronous termination.
Rejecting the converse inference that any ordinary State without outgoing Transitions is a FinalState or proves completion.
does_not_support: That pyfcstm terminated() denotes UML terminate-pseudostate entry, top-level FinalState completion, external asynchronous termination, or their disjunction.
That a named state such as FinalState is a UML FinalState without a native metamodel binding.
That one completed Region proves whole-machine completion when another top-level Region remains active.
Any issue-specific claim about which completion or termination behavior the author intended.
claim_to_source_matrix.project_operationalization: A gold property names its observed completion or termination concept and must provide a separately audited pyfcstm/backend mapping. Without that mapping, a completed backend Boolean cannot be promoted to an exact UML termination claim.

supports: Binding trace properties to an initial status, an ordered sequence of steps, environmental stimuli, and explicit observables.
Treating step semantics and side effects as part of the property meaning.
Rejecting trace comparisons that omit the semantic profile under which statuses are produced.

Any requirement-specific expected run.

claim_to_source_matrix.claim: Bounded model checking searches for counterexamples up to an explicit length k by SAT encoding; a satisfying encoding establishes a bounded counterexample, while absence of a counterexample at an arbitrary k is not an unbounded proof unless a completeness bound is established.

citation.title: Symbolic Model Checking without BDDs
citation.venue: Tools and Algorithms for the Construction and Analysis of Systems (TACAS 1999)

locator.access_level: Full institutional-repository copy of the conference paper verified.

short_quote.text: the bound is the maximal length of a counterexample

supports: Persisting the exact bound and distinguishing bounded from unbounded claims.
Using a completed satisfiable query as bounded counterexample evidence for the encoded model.
Returning UNKNOWN or bounded-only status when an UNSAT result lacks a justified completeness bound.
does_not_support: Treating no counterexample up to k as proof of an unbounded invariant or response property.
Inventing k from artifact size when the property requires a source-specified physical or semantic bound.
Assuming the SAT encoding faithfully represents the author artifact without a checked mapping.
Treating solver error, timeout, or incomplete replay as false.
claim_to_source_matrix.project_operationalization: Every BMC-backed gold row records finite horizon, unit, closed domain, encoded model identity, solver completion, and replay. False can close with a valid bounded witness; true is exact only with the protocol's declared completeness argument for that fragment.

claim_to_source_matrix.claim: A counterexample produced on an over-approximating abstract model may be spurious and must be checked for correspondence to an actual trace in the concrete model before it is reported as valid.

locator.access_level: Full institutional-repository copy of the conference paper verified.

short_quote.text: the abstract counterexample might not be valid. We say that such a counterexample is spurious.

supports: Checking a witness against the exact concrete artifact/model rather than trusting an abstract trace.
Treating failed concrete correspondence as invalid/spurious evidence rather than as a defect.
Recording the first mismatch between abstract and concrete traces when abstraction is involved.
does_not_support: That replay alone proves O/P equivalence or author-source attribution.
That a parser projection, compiler, or semantic adapter is faithful without a separate certificate.
That every non-abstract native trace requires CEGAR-style refinement.
That a valid execution trace necessarily proves the ledger issue as worded.
claim_to_source_matrix.project_operationalization: Track C accepts counterexample evidence only after exact artifact-hash binding and matching replay under the same semantic profile. Replay is necessary execution evidence, but source-to-property equivalence and mapping fidelity remain separate gates.

resolved_source_gaps.resolution: Dwyer is bounded to the exact IEEE Xplore Abstract section, Barr Definitions 2.6-2.8 are verified on printed page 510 of the IEEE PDF, and Beer is replaced by the FMSD 2001 journal article with its exact IBM Research Abstract section. project_operationalization_limitations.claim: The three internal tracks and pane5 evidence-based arbitration are project quality-control mechanisms; no measured improvement in predicate-gold validity or recovery of ground truth is claimed.
project_operationalization_limitations.reason: The cited literature motivates source normalization and directional oracle reasoning but does not prescribe or validate this reviewer architecture. The protocol therefore reports the workflow as an internal project operationalization, not an externally validated annotation method.

project_operationalization_limitations.claim: The positive-control construction is a project diagnostic intended to expose some wrong bindings and vacuous truths; it is not claimed to detect every such error or to prove O/P equivalence.
project_operationalization_limitations.reason: Beer establishes the vacuity problem, not the sensitivity or contamination resistance of this repaired-artifact control. Each control is audited locally, while general effectiveness remains unmeasured.

project_operationalization_limitations.claim: No wholesale semantic equivalence is claimed among UML, STATEMATE, ioco/LTS, pyfcstm, and the FCSTM/BMC backend.
project_operationalization_limitations.reason: The sources define different semantic objects and profiles. The protocol imports only proposition-specific clauses and requires explicit mapping evidence; the matrix is not evidence of wholesale semantic equivalence.
